---
title: Profile language
description: Store the admin language of each user in the database.
navigation:
  icon: i-lucide-languages
---

This feature stores the admin language of each user in the database. It plugs into the [i18n](/core/i18n) system of core through a locale driver.

## The data

`profiles.locale` is text and can be null. Null means **Automatic**: the user has not chosen a language, so the admin uses the browser language.

The check `profiles_locale_format` accepts any code that looks like `en` or `pt-BR`. It does not list the allowed languages, so a new language needs no migration. The route checks the code against `runtimeConfig.public.plutoI18n.adminLocales`.

The migration is `005_profile_locale.sql`.

## Why a function writes the column

`public.profiles` has no update policy. A policy that lets a user update their own row would also let them write `is_admin`.

So the function `public.set_my_locale(new_locale text)` is the only writer.

- It is `security definer` with an empty `search_path`.
- It updates the row where `id = auth.uid()` and sets only `locale` and `updated_at`.
- The migration revokes `execute` from `public` and `anon`, and grants it to `authenticated`.
- The migration adds no RLS policy.

A user reads their own row through the existing select policy.

## Routes

`GET /api/profile/locale` returns `{ locale: string | null }` for the calling user.

- A signed-out caller gets `{ locale: null }`.
- If the column does not exist yet, the route logs the error and returns `{ locale: null }`.

`POST /api/profile/locale` takes `{ locale: string | null }`.

| Case | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Signed out | 401 |
| Body does not match | 400 |
| Locale not in `adminLocales` | 400 |
| The function `set_my_locale` does not exist | 409 with the key `supabase.profile.migrationPending` |
| Any other error | 500 |
| Success | `{ locale }` |

## The client

The layer registers a `localeDriver` that calls the two routes. If a save fails, the language card on the Settings page shows the reason in a toast. The switch stays on the device, because core keeps it in a cookie.

Core's `pluto-auth-sync.client.ts` loads the stored language when a session appears. The plugin is client-only. A server `$fetch` does not forward the user cookies, so a server run would read no locale and clear the cookie.

## A site that did not apply migration 005

The language card still works, and the switch is kept in the cookie. The save returns 409, and the toast tells the admin to apply the pending migrations on `/admin/migrations`.
